claim: Blaxel sandboxes automatically shut down and stop billing active compute after 1-5 seconds of inactivity, metered down to the gigabyte-second, so idle agents cost nothing beyond snapshot/volume storage.
stance_target: auto-killing idle agents at the infrastructure/billing layer is a solved, productized pattern with sub-5-second granularity
quoted_support: They automatically spin up when you connect and shut down after a period of inactivity ranging between 1 to 5s. Pay only for the active seconds an agent is running code, not for the hours it sits idle.

claim: Blaxel's idle-detection/billing pipeline is fail-safe toward under-billing: it combines discrete lifecycle state-transition logs (STARTING/RUNNING/STOPPING/STOPPED) with continuous heartbeats specifically so that a missed heartbeat or lost log can only result in lost revenue for the vendor, never an over-charge to the customer.
stance_target: reliable idle-kill billing requires redundant signals (state logs + heartbeats), not a single event type
quoted_support: Any internal failure in our logging or heartbeat chain can only result in under-billing, never over-billing. A gap in our data is a loss for us, not our users.

claim: At fleet scale, usage-based agent billing requires dedicated real-time observability infrastructure (Blaxel combined Stripe for payments with the open-source OpenMeter for real-time usage tracking and threshold alerting) because standard payment platforms like Stripe lack real-time balance/consumption observability needed to prevent runaway spend.
stance_target: monitoring overhead for fleet-scale agent cost tracking requires purpose-built tooling beyond standard billing stacks
scope_conditions: Blaxel's production billing architecture, prepaid credits model
quoted_support: The real problem is that Stripe isn't an observability tool... OpenMeter gave us what Stripe lacked: real-time observability... It also provided consumption alerting through webhooks that fire when a user's consumption hits a certain threshold.
